title: Oncall shift digest and runbook TODOs (Zyra)
content:
Shift: 2026-05-05 19:00-03:00 PT (night)
Owner: Zyra Patel
Summary: quiet night overall, one sustained page around 22:13 (token-service latency spike) that resolved to degraded KV cache hit rate after a rolling autoscaler event. Follow-ups and runbook TODOs below.

Immediate timeline (notes to self)
- 22:10 alert: P99 token-gen > 850ms for ~6m, alerts aggregated by route token-service-prod.
- 22:12 paged oncall. Jumped into tracing (traces/token-service/2026-05-05T22:11Z) — saw cache miss ratio jump from 4% to 41%.
- 22:15 checked infra dashboards (grafana:/dashboards/infra/token-service): autoscaler triggered 3x worker replacements in 4m. New nodes came up with slightly different kernel (nv-5.17 vs nv-5.15) — possible driver mismatch?
- 22:20 rollout rollback to previous revision (route pinned) — latency returned to baseline by 22:24.
- Postmortem note: customer-facing requests saw elevated latency but no increased error rate.

Quick commands run / snippets
- kubectl get pods -n token-prod -l app=token-service -o wide (used to check node / kernel tags)
- curl -sS http://token-service/internal/health | jq .cache_stats (cache miss/hit snapshot)
- system journal grep on nodes (journalctl -u device-driver) showed GPU driver restart on one node at ~22:09 — collect node logs for cluster autoscaler correlation.

Short RCA (WIP)
- Probable trigger: autoscaler replaced nodes as part of stress scheduling, new node images had a driver that caused occasional cache warming failures -> spike in cache misses -> higher token latency.
- Why did autoscaler replace nodes? Need check: preemptible vs spot eviction? Scheduled maintenance? kubelet OOM?
- Why did new nodes get different kernel/driver? Image roll or manual image update? Check infra-change log.

Follow-ups (high priority)
- [ ] Open INC ticket and link traces + node logs (me) -> JIRA-INC-8732 (to create) – due 2026-05-07 EOD.
- [ ] Export node journal logs and attach to incident (assign: Elliot).
- [ ] Coordinate with infra-platform to verify image/driver roll (Maya to ping infra oncall).
- [ ] Add a temporary guard in autoscaler policy to avoid replacing >20% of pool within 10m for token-service pool (me + infra).

Runbook gaps I hit (notes to patch)
- Runbook step for token-service autoscaler events is sparse: no clear instruction to check kernel/driver tags on nodes. Add section: "validate node image and kernel version" with exact kubectl/jq commands.
- Missing checklist item: capture cache_stats snapshot and link to trace ID when opening incident.
- No rollback playbook for 'image mismatch' — add guidance: how to pin nodes to known-good AMI and trigger graceful drain/replace.

Draft runbook TODOs (what to add)
- Add snippet: kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, kernel: .status.nodeInfo.kernelVersion, image: .status.nodeInfo.osImage}'
- Add quick triage checklist:
  - Confirm if autoscaler triggered: kubectl describe hpa/hpa-token-service or check cluster-autoscaler logs
  - Get earliest trace ID for first elevated request (traces/token-service?start=...)
  - Snapshot cache_stats and redis/kv metrics, attach to incident
  - If node image mismatch: plan for rolling update to known AMI, or temporarily pin route to previous revision.

Nice-to-have follow-ups (medium priority)
- [ ] Add synthetic test for cache-warm path that runs after node join (CI job) -> reduces warmup-induced misses.
- [ ] Improve autoscaler telemetry to log node image id at scaling events.
- [ ] Create alert that detects sudden >10% increase in cache_miss_ratio across pool in 5m (low-noise threshold).

Open questions / to investigate
- Did cluster-autoscaler perform node replacement or was it a human-initiated action? Need audit logs.
- Does image pipeline occasionally roll images without changing tags? Check infra-pipeline PRs around 2026-05-05 21:00-22:30.
- Is there a correlation between token-service route traffic burst and underlying batch jobs? (check jobs-runbook)

Personal TODOs and reminders
- Draft the incident ticket text first (bullet points, attach trace + graphs) before morning sync.
- Connect with Maya and set up 30m sync for Monday morning (agenda: runbook patch + autoscaler safety fix).
- Remember to update runbook revision history with links to INC ticket and PR when done.

Random jottings (notes-to-self)
- Keep a copy of the curl/jq cache_stats command in clipboard.
- If I add synthetic test, put under infra/ci/nightly-small-tests.
- Check if similar cache spikes happened in past 90 days: grep "cache miss" in incidents archive.

End of shift checklist
- Leave quick summary in #sre-oncall with incident link and next steps.
- Mark handoff for morning oncall (Maya) with TODO list.

---
Small log entry for morning triage: create JIRA-INC-8732, add attachments, mention root-cause hypothesis and mitigation plan (autoscaler guard).

(End of scratchpad)
